Excluding the frontier region, where the num-ber of households changed often, the central region was probably the smallest scope of jurisdiction over which the governor had full and direct responsibility. The point of contact between the centralist and dualist perspectives sur-rounding the nature of commandants could be found in the distinction between the central region and the Y ŏngdong region indicated in the household register of Lelang Commandery. It appears that the comman-dant headquarters, unlike the centralist perspective, did not have a sepa-rate civil administrative function, such as assessing the number of house-holds, around the fourth year of Chuyuan, since the governor of the com-mandery kept count of the households in the seven Y ŏngdong counties along with the households in the counties in the central region. It is also difficult to assume that county-level civil administration was established in the frontier counties in the Former Han, allowing the gov-ernor of the commandery to rule over the whole commandery, simply based on the section on Tongokch ŏ from the Records of the Three King-doms, since that particular record was about the time period after the commandant headquarters of the Y ŏngdong region was abolished in the Dae-Jae Park 31 

sixth year of Jianwu (30 CE) and counties including Pullae, Hwary ŏ, and Okch ŏ became fiefdoms. In the record that indicates, “However, the of-fices of merit ( 功曹 ), registrar ( 主簿 ), ministries ( 諸曹 ) still remain to date in the fiefdom of Pullae, and these offices were undertaken by the people of Ye,” 46 the characters “ 至今 ” meaning “to date” refers to the time peri-od when the Records of the Three Kingdoms was compiled in Jin China (280s CE) or the Three Kingdoms period (220-265 CE). As a result, it is difficult to confirm whether civil administrative institu-tions such as ministries and offices of merit and registrar were established in Pullae during the Former Han. It is possible that the civil administrative institutions were established in counties after the role of the commandant headquarters was expanded or the commandant headquarters was abol-ished and the counties became fiefdoms. Therefore it is difficult to as-sume that the seven Y ŏngdong counties, where commandants were estab-lished in the Former Han, had been under centralized rule through county-level administration. While the governor of the commandery held administrative rule over the frontier region of Lelang Commandery, it seems that the frontier re-gion was governed separately from the central region where the comman-dant headquarters was not established. In other words, the governor’s administrative power inclusively reached the frontier region, but there were differences between the regions where the commandant headquar-ters was established and the regions without the commandant headquar-ters. Due to this multi-layered structure of the commandery, it seems that the household register of Lelang Commandery distinguishes between the central Lelang region and the Y ŏngdong region, where the commandant headquarters of the Eastern Section was established. Therefore the 25 counties in the household register of Lelang Commandery can be divided largely into the central region (18 counties), which have been marked as “kiho ,” and the frontier region of Y ŏngdong (seven counties), where the

## Regional Distinctions according to the Household Register of Lelang Commandery 

In the studies published since Son Y ŏngjong’s paper, scholars have di-vided the 25 counties of Lelang Commandery into four regions. As men-tioned earlier in this paper, Son asserted that seven counties from the sev-enth Taebang county to the 13th Hamja county were the seven counties of Daifang Commandery found in the “Treatise on Geography” in the Book of Jin , or in other words the region under the commandant headquarters of the Southern Section in Lelang Commandery during the Former Han, and distinguished the last seven counties from Tongi county as the seven Yŏngdong counties. Based on this grouping, the six counties (Chos ŏncounty to Tunyu county) and five counties (Sus ŏng county to T’any ŏlcounty) before and after the seven counties of Daifang Commandery (commandant headquarters of the Southern Section), were also grouped separately, so that all 25 counties were divided into four regions—Central Lelang, Southern Lelang, Northern Lelang, and seven Y ŏngdong counties. As of now, it makes most sense to divide the 25 counties in the house-hold register of Lelang Commandery into two groups—the seven counties of Y ŏngdong, which were separately inscribed on the third wooden tablet; and the 18 counties in the central regions of Lelang, inscribed on the first and second wooden tablets. This regional grouping scheme is also related to the nature of kiho discussed in the previous sections. The term kiho in the household register of Lelang Commandery refers to the 18 counties in the central regions of Lelang, excluding the Y ŏngdong region. The regional grouping of Lelang Commandery as seen in the household register is related to the multi-level ruling structure of the frontier coun-ties. The frontier counties seem to have been governed under the multi-level ruling scheme involving both the governor and commandant. The frontier regions in the Han dynasty were equipped with elaborate defense systems, consisting of the commandant headquarters 都尉府 (comman-dants 都尉 ), companies 候官 (commanding officers of companies 候),

The domicile of lower ranking officials who worked in defense facilities in the frontier regions was the nearest county, and the families of such lower ranking officials resided there as well. 53 The soldiers in the frontier regions were supplied from all across the inte-rior provinces within Han China, while lower ranking officers and gov-ernment officials were usually local residents. 54 Due to these circumstances, it is difficult to argue that the relationship between defense facilities and nearby counties had been strictly divided into the former overseeing military matters while the latter oversaw civil affairs. ## Conclusion 

As examined in this paper, the household register of Lelang Command-ery confirms that the number of households in the 18 main counties and in the seven Y ŏngdong counties were calculated separately. The term kiho at the end of the household register was a term used to specify a certain number of households of the 18 main counties. This term implies that the 18 counties were under the governor’s direct control, while the seven Yŏngdong counties were under the control of the commandant headquar-ters of the Eastern Section. However, the fact that the households of all 25 counties, including the seven Y ŏngdong counties, were included in the household register shows that the Y ŏngdong region was also under the control of the governor of Lelang. In other words, the seven Y ŏngdong counties were areas that were under the control of both the governor of Lelang and the comman-dant of the Eastern Section. In previous studies, scholars have debated the central government’s means to govern the seven Y ŏngdong counties: some argue that the ruling system of the seven counties had been centralized under the governor of Lelang, while others assert that the commandant of the Eastern Section ruled over them. However, an examination of the household register shows that a multi-level ruling structure had been implemented, in which the seven Y ŏngdong counties were ruled by both the governor of Lelang and the commandant of the Eastern Section. # A New Approach to the Household Register of Lelang Commandery 

Dae-Jae Park 

The household register of Lelang Commandery first revealed in North Korea in 2006 is comprised of wooden tablets that contain detailed information on the number of households of 25 counties in Lelang Commandery. By exploring the nature of kiho (其戶 ), an item found at the end of the household register of Lelang Commandery, this study illustrates the fact that there were regional distinctions between the 18 counties of the central region and the seven counties of Y ŏngdong. 

Kiho refers to the households in eighteen counties, of the total households in Le-lang Commandery, excluding the seven counties of Y ŏngdong. This demonstrates that the 18 counties in the central region had been under the direct control of the governor of Lelang, while the seven Y ŏngong counties were under the jurisdiction of the commandant headquarters of the Eastern Section, an office that was estab-lished separately to govern the seven counties. At the same time, this article also notes that the number of households in all 25 counties of Lelang Commandery was recorded together on the document, as this meant that the administrative ju-risdiction of the governor of Lelang included all 25 counties, including the seven Yŏngdong counties. Since the commandant headquarters of the Eastern Section were a military office under the command of the governor of Lelang Commandery, the seven Y ŏngdong counties were also under the governor’s administrative con-trol. Therefore the seven Y ŏngdong counties can be understood as a region gov-erned indirectly by the governor of Lelang and directly by the commandant head-quarters of the Eastern Section. 

Keywords: Lelang Commandery ( 樂浪郡 ), household register ( 戶口簿 ), seven counties of Y ŏngdong ( 嶺東 7縣), inner commandery ( 內郡 ), frontier com-mandery ( 邊郡 ), section commandants ( 部都尉 ), commandery commandant (郡都尉 ), governor of Lelang ( 樂浪太守 ), Commandant of the Eastern Section (東部都尉 )A New Approach to the Household Register of Lelang ( 樂浪 ) Commandery 46

# 낙랑군 호구부에 대한 새로운 접근 

박대재 (고려대 한국사학과 교수 )2006 년 북한에서 처음 공개된 樂浪郡 戶口簿는 기원전 45 년 낙랑군 소속 25 개

縣의 현별 호구수를 상세히 기록한 集計 木簡이다 . 이 글에서는 낙랑군 호구부 말미에 기록된 ‘其戶 ’의 성격에 새롭게 접근함으로써 , 낙랑군 25 개현 내에 本郡 18 

현과 嶺東 7현 사이의 지역구분이 있었다는 사실을 밝혀보았다 . ‘ 其戶 ’는 낙랑군 

전체 호구수 (凡戶 ) 가운데 영동 7현을 제외한 本郡 18 현의 호구수만 따로 집계한 

것이다 . 이것은 본군 18 현 지역이 太守가 직접 관할한 지역이며 , 나머지 영동 7현은 별도로 설치된 東部都尉의 관할 아래에 있었던 지역이라는 사실을 시사해준다 .

그러면서도 호구부에는 영동 7현을 포함해 낙랑군 소속 25 개현의 호구수를 일괄 

기록되어 있다는 점도 아울러 주목해 보았다 . 이것은 樂浪太守의 행정 관할 범위 가 영동 7현 지역까지 모두 포괄한다는 것을 의미하는 것이다 . 동부도위 역시 郡太守의 통솔 하에 있던 郡官이라는 점에서 , 영동 7현도 태수의 행정적 관할 범위 에 포함되어 있었던 것이다 . 결국 영동 7현은 樂浪太守의 간접지배와 東部都尉의 

직접지배가 중층적으로 시행되었던 지역이라고 이해할 수 있다 .

주제어 : 樂浪郡 , 戶口簿 , 嶺東 7縣, 內郡 , 邊郡 , 部都尉 , 郡都尉 , 樂浪太守 , 東部 都尉

20.title: A great sage of the nation who revitalized the 5 000-year-long history of the nation - KIM IL SUNG UNIVERSITY
20.description: The great leaders Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il, who possessed of the most ardent patriotic idea, were deeply aware of the importance and significance of the historical study of Tangun and Ancient Joson in correctly clarifying and systematizing the 5 000-year-long history of the nation, and led the historians and archaeologists to conduct properly the study of Tangun and Ancient Korea.
20.content:
Dr. Associate Prof. Jong Kwang Su, Faculty of Economics,

Kim Il Sung
University

2021.9.23.

The great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung said:

**"The excavation of Tangun's Tomb and the discovery of his remains is the great victory of archaeology in our country and an immense pride of the Korean nation."**

The great leaders Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il, who possessed of the most ardent patriotic idea, were deeply aware of the importance and significance of the historical study of Tangun and Ancient Joson in correctly clarifying and systematizing the 5 000-year-long history of the nation, and led the historians and archaeologists to conduct properly the study of Tangun and Ancient Korea.

The great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung gave precious instructions to study the history of Tangun and Ancient Korea on dozens of occasions in Juche 82 (1993) and Juche 83 (1994), the last moments of his great life.

The first and foremost task in correctly elucidating the history of Tangun and Ancient Korea was to clarify the reality of Tangun Mausoleum, the founder of the nation-building of Ancient Korea. At that time, however, scholars specializing in history, obsessed with the mistaken thought and view that Tangun was only a mythical man, were completely ignorant of Tangun's tomb in Kangdong Town, Kangdong County, Pyongyang, and so they didn't even give a thought of unearthing it.

On January 8, Juche 82 (1993), the great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung instructed officials to discover the tomb of Tangun and restore it to its original state, saying that in order to correctly formulate the history of the Korean nation from the Juche-oriented standpoint, it was necessary to correct the history of Tangun and ancient Korea which had been distorted by the Japanese imperialists in the past.

There were not many remains during its excavation as they were stolen by the Japanese imperialists before liberation, but notably there were the bones of two people and the gold-plated pieces of crown.

On receiving the report, the great leader gave the officials concerned an instruction that they should perform scientific and chronological investigation for the fragments of crowns and those bones.

The great leader Comrade Kim Jong Il, who is creditably carrying forward the patriotic intention of the great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung, took benevolent measures to have the historical scientists and archaeologists timely provided the state-of-art equipment necessary for dating human bones unearthed at Tangun Mausoleum.

On September 10, Juche 82 (1993), the great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung briefed proudly the members of the delegation of the General Association of Korean Residents in Japan (ChongRyon) on their visit to the socialist motherland about the successful unearthing the mausoleum of Tangun by our archaeologists.

Saying that our ancestors had worshipped Tangun for a long time, regarding him as a mythical being, the great leader said that in the period of the feudal Joson dynasty people had performed memorial service of Tangun until the occupation of Korea by Japanese imperialists.

He said with great emotion that the discovery of the mausoleum of Tangun and the confirmation of the 5000-year-long remains of Tangun show that Tangun, once recognized as a mythical being, was really and archaeologically proved to be a real man in history and that our country was a civilized country with a 5 000-year-long history, and that we could have a new understanding of Tangun based on scientific grounds.

Indeed, the great leaders Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il were the peerless patriots and great sages of the nation who glorified the nation's history spanning 5 000 years and found the ancestral father of nation-building and the benevolent teacher of our people.

They also paid deep attention to the work of conducting the restoration of the tombs of Tangun along with the excavation of the tombs of Tangun and giving wide publicity to the achievements made in the study of the tombs at home and abroad.

While guiding a consultative meeting on the restoration of the mausoleum of Tangun on Sept. 25, Juche 82 (1993), the great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung gave precious instructions for studying the history of Tangun and Ancient Korea and giving publicity to it. On the same day, on the basis of the historical relics and remains newly discovered in Tangun and Ancient Korea, he pointed out that the time-honored history of 5 000 years and the homogeneity of the nation should make public all over the world, and the report on the unearthing of the Mausoleum of King Tangun be introduced widely through the newspapers including Rodong Sinmun and broadcasts, and an academic symposium be organized to widely introduce it home and abroad.

Accordingly, the report of King Tangun's Mausoleum entitled "Demonstration of 5 000-year-long history and homogeneity of the nation" was published in Rodong Sinmun on October 2, Juche 82 (1993).

The great leaders Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il led the work to successfully reconstruct the tomb of King Tangun as a mausoleum of the ancestral father of the nation in keeping with the successful excavation and dating of the tomb of King Tangun.

On September 27, Juche 82(1993), the great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung visited the Mausoleum of King Tangun in Kangdong County, together with officials and historians concerned, and gave instructions in terms of its preservation, looking around the mausoleum of Tangun, its monument and stone sculpture of tiger.

Saying that the King Tangun's mausoleum should be located in a good place and reconstructed well, he invited the officials to get into his car, remarking that he had pinpointed one location in mind.

He climbed a beautiful hill at the foot of Mt. Taebak and said that it would be the best place for the reconstruct of the mausoleum of King Tangun.

The site set by the great leader was an excellent place in many aspects such as the feature and location of the mountain.

With such noble love for the nation, the great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung personally set the site for the reconstruction of the mausoleum and gave detailed guidance to make sure that it could be wonderfully built as a monumental edifice in the era of the Workers' Party.

On October 20, Juche 82(1993), the great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung held a consultative meeting of officials concerned with the reconstruction of the Mausoleum of King Tangun and made a historic speech titled "On the Direction of Reconstruction of the Mausoleum of King Tangun".

That day, the great leader Kim Il Sung said that the reconstruction of the Mausoleum of King Tangun had a great significance as ours is a long historical country with a history of 5,000 years, a homogeneous nation which has inherited one blood vessel since the birth of our nation, and that Pyongyang, the capital of the revolution, is the original birthplace of Tangun as well as Korean nation.

Noting the Mausoleum of King Tongmyong, the founder of Koguryo, is the tomb of the primitive father of the Korean nation, the great leader pointed out that the Mausoleum of Tangun be larger and higher than the Mausoleum of King Tongmyong, the founder of Koguryo, and its construction be completed in a pyramid-making way with stone layers rather than earth as used in the case of Mausoleum of King Tongmyong.

In the last period of his life, too, the great leader acquainted himself with the construction of the Mausoleum of King Tangun and took necessary measures and personally examined the plan for reconstructing the mausoleum and approved it.

During the great mourning period when the whole country writhed in the agony of the demise of the father of the nation, the great leader Comrade Kim Jong Il led the Korean people and the builders of the Mausoleum of King Tangun to convert their agony into the great willpower and courage to turn out in the implementation of reconstructing the Mausoleum of King Tangun, the behest of the great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung.

He also sent a powerful construction group needed for the construction and took all measures, giving priority to supplying modern machinery and equipment and building materials.

Shortly after the inauguration of the Mausoleum of King Tangun, the great leader Comrade Kim Jong Il visited the Mausoleum of King Tangun, which was built as a monumental edifice in the era of the Workers' Party of Korea, on October 29, Juche 83 (1994).

That day, the great leader Comrade Kim Jong Il expressed great satisfaction over the splendid reconstruction of the Mausoleum of King Tangun and recollected with deep emotion the undying exploits performed by the great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung for the reconstruction of the Mausoleum of King Tangun. He said that the great leader visited Tangun, the ancestral father of the Korean nation, who had been handed down as a myth for a long time, and saw to it that the Mausoleum of King Tangun be reconstructed magnificently.

His historic field guidance to the Mausoleum of King Tangun marked an epochal event in ever glorifying the noble patriotic exploits of the great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung and conveying the time-honored history and brilliant cultural traditions of the Korean nation down through generations.

The respected Comrade Kim Jong Un, who is successfully carrying forward the noble patriotic cause of the great leaders, in a talk to senior officials of the Central Committee of the Workers' Party of Korea on Oct. 24, Juche 103 (2014), said with deep emotion the undying feats of great leaders Kim Il sung and Kim Jong Il who devoted themselves to the reconstruction of the mausoleum of King Tangun.

The respected Comrade Kim Jong Un told officials that the great leader Comrade Kim Jong Il energetically guided the reconstruction of the Mausoleum of King Tangun which the great leader Comrade Kim Il Sung personally initiated and paid deep attention to, as an important undertaking for implementing the behest, and that it is a great auspicious event of the Korean nation and a brilliant victory of the policy of protecting the national heritage that the Mausoleum of King Tangun was splendidly remodeled thanks to the noble patriotism and wise guidance of the great leaders.

Upon receiving the words of the respected Comrade Kim Jong Un reflecting his boundless loyalty to the Great Leaders and noble love and devotion for the country and people, the social scientists burnt their hearts with the patriotic will to cherish Kim Jong Il's patriotism and add luster to the history of the Korean nation recovered and glorified by the peerlessly great men under his seasoned leadership.

24.title: Tomb of King Tongmyong
24.content:
[![Image 1: Tomb of King Gongmin in North Korea with stone sculptures on the tomb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong.jpg/250px-Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong.jpg)

The tomb of King Tongmyŏng, Pyongyang.

The **Tomb of King Tongmyŏng** ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"):동명왕릉; [Hanja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanja "Hanja"):東明王陵), also known as the **Tomb of King Dongmyeong**, is a [mausoleum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausoleum "Mausoleum") located in near Ryongsan Village, [Ryokpo-guyok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryokpo-guyok "Ryokpo-guyok"), [Pyongyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyongyang "Pyongyang"), [North Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea "North Korea"). One of the tombs is the royal tomb of [Jumong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jumong "Jumong") (58–19 BC), the founder of the ancient [Goguryeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goguryeo "Goguryeo") Kingdom, the northernmost of the [Three Kingdoms of Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Kingdoms_of_Korea "Three Kingdoms of Korea"). King Jumong was given the posthumous name of King [Dongmyeong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dongmyeong_of_Goguryeo "Dongmyeong of Goguryeo"). In total, there are 63 individual tombs of the period. The area around Dongmyeong's grave contains at least fifteen known tombs believed to belong to various [vassal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vassal "Vassal") lords. The tomb has achieved [World Heritage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") status as part of the [Complex of Goguryeo Tombs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goguryeo_tombs "Goguryeo tombs") inscribed by [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO") in 2004 under Criteria (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) covering an area of 233 hectares (580 acres) with a buffer zone of 1,701 hectares (4,200 acres).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-Unesco-1) A unique feature of it and the other extant tombs in the area are the wall paintings depicting blossoming [lotuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_plants_known_as_lotus "List of plants known as lotus"), indicative of [Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism "Buddhism") practiced and perhaps prevalent in [Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea "Korea") around 277 BC to 668 AD.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-Unesco-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-Advisory-2)

[![Image 2: Tombs of King and Queen Seondeok of Silla in a grove](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/King_Tongmyong_mausoleum_tumuli.jpg/250px-King_Tongmyong_mausoleum_tumuli.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:King_Tongmyong_mausoleum_tumuli.jpg)

Royal burial tumuli within the mausoleum complex.

**Korean name**
[Chosŏn'gŭl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangul "Hangul")동명왕릉
[Hancha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanja "Hanja")[東](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%9D%B1 "wikt:東")[明](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%98%8E "wikt:明")[王](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E7%8E%8B "wikt:王")[陵](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E9%99%B5 "wikt:陵")
[Revised Romanization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revised_Romanization_of_Korean "Revised Romanization of Korean")_Dongmyeongwangneung_
[McCune–Reischauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCune%E2%80%93Reischauer "McCune–Reischauer")_Tongmyŏngwangrŭng_

The sacred site was built when [King Jangsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jangsu_of_Goguryeo "Jangsu of Goguryeo") transferred his capital from the [Hwando Mountain Fortress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hwando "Hwando") to [Pyongyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyongyang "Pyongyang") in 427 AD. The Royal Tomb of King Dongmyeong is one of 63 tombs that exist in five zones of [North Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea "North Korea"). The construction of all these tombs is dated to the 5th and 6th centuries. Its history is traced to Goguryeo Kingdom which existed between 277 BC to 668 AD, initially in [Huanren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huanren_Manchu_Autonomous_County "Huanren Manchu Autonomous County"), [Liaoning Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liaoning "Liaoning") in China. It was then shifted to [Gungnae Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gungnae "Gungnae") in 3 AD in [Ji'an](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ji%27an,_Jilin "Ji'an, Jilin"), [Jilin Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jilin "Jilin"), of China and later moved to the [Mount Taesong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taesongsan "Taesongsan") area, in Pyongyang, in 427 AD. Its final location was to the present location at Jangan Castle in the center of Pyongyang.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-Unesco-1) Goguryeo had five ancient tribes each with its own ancestral tomb observing rites celebrated during the tenth month of every year by performing the _tongmyong_ ("petition to the east") which is the worship of a heavenly deity named Susin.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHall1993362-3)[Kiringul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiringul "Kiringul") is situated 200 metres (660 ft) from the Yongmyong Temple in Moran Hill in Pyongyang. It is a rectangular rock which is carved with the inscription 'Unicorn Lair'. Based on the discovery of the King's unicorn lair, archaeologists of the History Institute of the [DPRK Academy of Social Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Academy_of_Social_Sciences_(North_Korea)&action=edit&redlink=1 "Academy of Social Sciences (North Korea) (page does not exist)")([ko](https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EC%82%AC%ED%9A%8C%EA%B3%BC%ED%95%99%EC%9B%90 "ko:사회과학원")) inferred that Pyongyang was the capital city of [Ancient Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Korea "History of Korea") and concurrently of the [Goguryeo Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goguryeo "Goguryeo").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-Lair-4) In 1697, during the era of [Sukjong of Joseon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukjong_of_Joseon "Sukjong of Joseon"), the king endorsed a proposal to annually repair the Tomb of King Dongmyeong.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-Tangun1994-5)

This and other tombs came to be publicised only after 1905, when Korea was [occupied by the Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea_under_Japanese_rule "Korea under Japanese rule"). The Japanese experts were instrumental in carrying out scientific research and documentation of the tombs from 1911 to the 1940s.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-Unesco-1) The original tombs had been ransacked by tomb hunters and were found by the [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan") archaeologists during excavations carried out in 1941. After excavations it was renovated for political reasons.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPortal2005111-6)

The UNESCO recognition in 2004 for the tombs was accorded under: Criterion i for the artistic elegance of the wall paintings; Criterion ii as it brings out the burial practice of Koguryo which had an influence on other cultures in the region including Japan; Criterion iii as the wall paintings represent the history, religious beliefs, and customs of the people; and Criterion iv for providing a burial typology.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-Unesco-1)

The legend behind the King's birth is told in the third-century Chinese historical text _[Weilüe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weil%C3%BCe "Weilüe")_, which is now mostly lost. According to the legend the chambermaid of the Queen became pregnant when she was struck by a bolt of lightning. Then the King fearing that it was a supernatural event which could harm him got the baby thrown into the pigsty. However, the baby survived on account of the breath support provided by the pigs. The baby was then thrown into a horse stable where he survived. Then realizing that the child was a divinity the King ordered his mother to bring him up. He was given the name _Dongmyeong_ (Eastern Light) considering the events which led to his birth. He then went to build his own kingdom after overcoming all obstacles and attempts made on his life. He then declared himself the King of [Buyeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buyeo "Buyeo").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHyung_Il_Pai2000467-7)

Political importance
--------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Political importance")]

For more information about the North Korean ideology, see [Juche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juche "Juche").

One of two important rituals was instituted during the reign of [Onjo of Baekje](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onjo_of_Baekje "Onjo of Baekje") that involved Dongmyeong; the first stressed the royal family's connections with the [Buyeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buyeo "Buyeo") peoples of [Manchuria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchuria "Manchuria") through the presentations of sacrifices at a shrine dedicated to Dongmyeong.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-8)

The era of the Kingdom of Goguryeo is of particular interest for the North Korean government.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTELankov200744-9) According to [Andrei Lankov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrei_Lankov "Andrei Lankov"), in the early 1970s, [Kim Jong Il](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Jong_Il "Kim Jong Il") reportedly pointed to "a major shortcoming of North Korean archaeology: archaeologists had failed to locate the tomb of King Tongmyŏng".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTELankov200744-45-10) In 1974, North Korean archaeologists produced the required tomb which was duly 'restored' and became a tourist attraction. [[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTELankov200745,_80-11) Although it was initially an authentic Goguryeo tomb known under the reference "Jinpari Tomb n°10",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTEYonhap_News_Agency2003500-12) there is no further evidence that this tomb is King Dongmyeong's.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTELankov200780-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPortal2005112%E2%80%9313-14)

The alleged discovery of the burial place of the founding monarch of the Kingdom of Goguryeo was followed by an extensive "restoration" during the 1980s.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTEYonhap_News_Agency2003500-12) The reconstruction process entailed the complete removal of all original buildings, structures, and monuments in order to create a new, white marble tomb.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-Kim-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-King-16) On 14 May 1993, the opening ceremony of the newly built tomb was attended by [Kim Il Sung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Il_Sung "Kim Il Sung"). Kim also wrote the calligraphy on the [stele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stele "Stele") that is erected at the tomb and which has the name of the King of Buyeo inscribed on it.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHyung_Il_Pai2000467-7) King Dongmyeong's tomb is of national heritage and its rebuilding and upkeep has been the responsibility of the state. Kim II-sung personally monitored the rebuilding of the tomb with funds provisioned by the state to make it “a historical cultural heritage to be handed down to the generation to come.”[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-Kim1997-17)

In 2002, coins of 10 [North Korean won](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korean_won "North Korean won") denomination were issued depicting the tomb of the King.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTECuhajMichael2012486-18)

Architecture and fittings
-------------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Architecture and fittings")]

The mausoleum is a 11.5 m (38 ft)-high [tumulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumulus "Tumulus") bordered at the base with stone blocks. Each side of the tumulus is 34 m (112 ft) long.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-19) The tomb has a 22 m 2 (240 sq ft) pyramidal inner chamber, a front chamber and a gallery made with stones. The chamber faces southwest.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-20) The renovated tomb of the king is the most prominent tomb and is one among the 20 tombs in [Chinpa Village.](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chinpari&action=edit&redlink=1 "Chinpari (page does not exist)") The current tomb complex is quite modern.

The Royal Tomb of King Dongmyeong and the Three Tombs of Kangso have mural paintings. The Tomb of King Dongmyeong has Goguryeo murals which are known for its rich color and tone. The wall paintings found in the tomb were of Buddhist themes, namely the lotus, and the animal depictions in the ceiling and walls of the tombs. The murals depict, realistically in a three-dimensional form, the daily life scenes of people such as women dancing, warriors getting trained, birds flying in the sky covered with clouds, dragons, fish swimming in rivers, and wild life.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-Unesco-1) The frescoes in the tomb depict lotuses in blossom with other religious ornamentation which bring out the traditional Buddhist ethos only and not the four traditional images of the constellations as in the Chinese tombs. This is inferred to represent the paradise in Buddhist religious parlance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHall1993362-3) The tomb has an inscription which substantiates the fact that it was a sacred site for festival rites. These consisted of the worship of mother earth and also livestock; the former is a south Asian rite while the latter is a shamanistic form of worship.

[![Image 3: Asian courtyard with a multi-tiered pagoda in the center and two monks walking towards the temple at opposite sides](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Chongrung_Temple.jpg/250px-Chongrung_Temple.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chongrung_Temple.jpg)

Chongrung Buddhist temple next to the Tomb of King Tongmyŏng

The grounds include a large grassy area which was one of the venues for the [13th World Festival of Youth and Students](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13th_World_Festival_of_Youth_and_Students "13th World Festival of Youth and Students").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarrold2004186-21)

The Buddhist monastery, discovered in 1978, is located about 120 metres (390 ft) from the tomb and was inferred as the monastery built by King Changsu (413–91) after the capital was moved to Pyongyang in 427 AD. The inscriptions found here proclaim that Changsu was the chief monk who conducted the rites at the tomb and also in the Buddhist monastery nearby. It has three halls surrounding the walls of a pagoda which is similar to Japanese temples built in later years, suggesting that the Buddhism culture of Goguryeo has also permeated to Japan. Goguryeo itself has been influenced by the Chinese Buddhism of the [Northern Dynasties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_and_Southern_dynasties#Northern_dynasties "Northern and Southern dynasties").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHall1993362-3)

### Chongrŭngsa Buddhist temple

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Chongrŭngsa Buddhist temple")]

The complex also houses the rebuilt [Chongrŭngsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chongr%C5%ADngsa&action=edit&redlink=1 "Chongrŭngsa (page does not exist)") Buddhist temple, where funeral services were held for the deceased monarch. The temple, whose foundations were excavated in 1974, was rebuilt to mark the 2,300th anniversary of Tongmyŏng's birth.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomb_of_King_Tongmyong#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHall1993362-3)

###### Complex of Koguryo Tombs

The property includes several group and individual tombs - totalling about 30 individual tombs - from the later period of the Koguryo Kingdom, one of the strongest kingdoms in nowadays northeast China and half of the Korean peninsula between the 3rd century BC to 7th century AD. The tombs, many with beautiful wall paintings, are almost the only remains of this culture. Only about 90 out of more than 10,000 Koguryo tombs discovered in China and Korea so far, have wall paintings. Almost half of these tombs are located on this site and they are thought to have been made for the burial of kings, members of the royal family and the aristocracy. These paintings offer a unique testimony to daily life of this period.

Description is available under license [CC-BY-SA IGO 3.0](https://whc.unesco.org/en/licenses/6)

###### Ensemble des tombes de Koguryo

Ce site comprend de nombreuses tombes, en groupes ou isolées (une trentaine), datant de la dernière période du royaume de Koguryo, l’un des royaumes les plus puissants de la Chine du nord-est et de la moitié de la péninsule coréenne entre le IIIe siècle av. J.-C. et le VIIe siècle apr. J.-C. Ces tombes, dont beaucoup sont ornées de splendides peintures murales, constituent presque les seuls vestiges laissés par cette culture. Sur les quelque 10 000 tombes de Koguryo découvertes jusqu’à présent en Chine et en Corée, 90 seulement comportent des peintures murales. Environ la moitié d’entre elles sont situées sur ce site ; on pense qu’elles étaient destinées aux rois ainsi qu’aux membres de la famille royale et de la noblesse. Ces peintures offrent un témoignage unique de la vie quotidienne de l’époque.

Description is available under license [CC-BY-SA IGO 3.0](https://whc.unesco.org/en/licenses/6)

###### مجموعة مقابر الكوغوريو

يتضمن هذا الموقع عدداً من المقابر المجتمعة أو المنفردة (التي يبلغ عددها الثلاثين) العائدة الى المرحلة الأخيرة من مملكة كوغوريوالتي كانت تعتبر من أقوى ممالك شمال شرق الصين ونصف شبه الجزيرة الكورية بين القرن الثالث قبل الميلاد والسابع ميلادي. وتعدّ هذه المقابر التي تزيّن الكثير منها لوحات جدارية مذهلة الآثار الوحيدة المتبقية من هذه الثقافة. ومن بين 10000 قبر تم اكتشافه حتى اليوم في الصين وكوريا، 90 قبرا فقط تحوي لوحات جدارية يقبع نصفها في هذا الموقع وسط اعتقاد سائد بأنها كانت مخصصة للملوك وأعضاء الأسرة الملكية والنبلاء. وتمثل هذه اللوحات شاهداً فريداً على الحياة اليومية السائدة في تلك الحقبة.

###### 高句丽古墓群

墓群包括几组墓葬和一些独立的墓葬，共计约30座，是公元前3世纪至公元7世纪中国东北部和朝鲜半岛一半地区最强大的帝国之一——高句丽帝国后期的古墓，多以精美的壁画装饰，几乎是高句丽文化唯一的遗迹。迄今为止，在中国和朝鲜发现的10 000多座高句丽古墓中只有90座古墓绘有壁画。其中半数以上就在该遗址，被认为是高句丽帝王、皇室成员或贵族的墓葬。这些壁画以独特的方式反映了当时的日常生活。

source: UNESCO/CPE

###### Комплекс гробниц Когурё

В комплекс входит несколько групп гробниц и отдельные гробницы – всего порядка 30 захоронений, которые относятся к позднему периоду существования государства Когурё, являясь ценнейшими свидетельствами этой культуры. Только около 90 гробниц Когурё из более чем 10 тыс., обнаруженных в целом в Китае и Корее к настоящему времени, имеют настенные росписи. Почти половина таких гробниц находится в пределах данного комплекса. Гробницы, как полагают, были сооружены для захоронения царей, членов царских семей и аристократии.

source: UNESCO/CPE

###### Conjunto de tumbas de Koguryo

Este sitio está integrado por un conjunto de 30 tumbas, agrupadas o aisladas, que datan de la época del Reino de Koguryo. El territorio de este reino, que fue uno de los más poderosos de la región entre los siglos III a. C. y VII a.C., se extendió por el nordeste de China y la mitad de la península coreana. Las tumbas son prácticamente los únicos vestigios de esta cultura y algunas de ellas poseen magníficas pinturas murales. De las 10.000 sepulturas del periodo koguryo descubiertas en China y Corea hasta la fecha, solamente 90 poseen pinturas murales. La mitad de las tumbas decoradas se hallan en este sitio y se cree que fueron construidas para albergar los despojos mortales de los soberanos, miembros de la familia real y personajes de la aristocracia koguryo. Las pinturas murales representan un testimonio excepcional de la vida cotidiana de la época.

source: UNESCO/CPE 

Description is available under license [CC-BY-SA IGO 3.0](https://whc.unesco.org/en/licenses/6)

###### 高句麗古墳群

ピョンヤン付近にあるこの遺産は、高句麗王国中・後期の63基の古墳からなる。高句麗王国は、紀元前1世紀にかけて栄えた、最強の王国の一つである。古墳の多くに残るう美しい壁画は、高句麗文化を現在に伝える貴重なものといってよい。1万を超える高句麗の古墳のうち、90の壁画古墳が現在までに中国と北朝鮮で発見されている。これらの古墳の半分近くが、今回登録された地域に位置している。壁画には4～5世紀頃の生活風習や高松塚古墳のものと似た女性像が描かれたものなどがある。

source: [NFUAJ](https://www.unesco.or.jp/activities/isan/worldheritagelist/)

###### Graftombecomplex van Koguryo

Het graftombecomplex van Koguryo bestaat uit groeps- en individuele graven – 30 individuele graven in totaal – uit de latere periode van het Koguryo koninkrijk. Van deze cultuur zijn bijna alleen de graven overgebleven. Ongeveer 90 van de meer dan 10.000 Koguryo graftombes die in China en Korea zijn ontdekt, hebben muurschilderingen. Bijna de helft van deze beschilderde tombes bevindt zich in het graftombecomplex. Men denkt dat ze gemaakt zijn voor de begrafenis van koningen, leden van de koninklijke familie en de aristocratie. De schilderijen geven een uniek beeld van het dagelijks leven in deze periode.

Source: [unesco.nl](http://unesco.nl/erfgoed/graftombecomplex-van-koguryo)

Outstanding Universal Value
---------------------------

**Brief synthesis**

Koguryo was one of the strongest kingdoms in northeast China and half of the Korean peninsula between the 3rd century BC and the 7th century AD. The best known cultural heritage remains of this kingdom are the tombs, built of stone and covered by stone or earthen mounds. These tombs, from the middle period of the kingdom, many with beautiful wall paintings, are the representative remains of this culture. About 100 out of more than 10,000 Koguryo tombs discovered in Democratic People’s Republic of Korea and China to date are decorated with wall paintings, some 80 of which are in the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea. Among the Koguryo tombs identified in Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, 63 individual tombs including 16 tombs with wall paintings are included in the inscribed property.

The Complex of Koguryo Tombs is a serial property and includes several groups and individual tombs situated mainly at the foot of mountains and some in villages. Located in Pyongyang and surrounding provinces, the tombs are thought to have been made for the burial of kings, members of the royal family and the aristocracy.

There are several types of tombs included in the property, based on the number of burial chambers – single chamber, two chambers, and multi-chambers with side chambers. They represent the full range of the Koguryo tomb typology and showcase the best examples of this construction technology. The tombs are monumental, stone-chambered earthen mounds that were skillfully constructed with ingenious ceiling designs to support the heavy weight above. The technology employed represented a unique, creative and long-sought engineering solution to the technical problems posed by underground tomb construction.

The wall paintings constitute masterpieces of the art of wall painting. The subject matter of the wall paintings of the tombs offers unique evidence of the richness and complexity of the now-vanished Koguryo culture, portraying the costumes, food, residential life and burial customs, as well as religious practices and imagery associated with Buddhism, Taoism and the Four Deities.

The Complex of Koguryo Tombs represents an exceptional testimony to the Koguryo culture, its burial customs, daily life and beliefs. The special burial customs of this culture had an important influence on other cultures in the region, including those of Japan.

**Criterion (i):** The wall paintings of the Koguryo tombs are masterpieces of the culture and period of the Koguryo kingdom; the construction of the tombs demonstrates ingenious engineering solutions.

**Criterion (ii):** The special burial customs of the Koguryo culture had an important influence on other cultures in the region, including Japan.

**Criterion (iii):** The Koguryo tombs are an exceptional testimony of the Koguryo culture, its burial customs as well as its daily life and beliefs.

**Criterion (iv):** The Complex of Koguryo Tombs is an important example of burial typology.

**Integrity**

The serial property, which is scattered across the northwest part of the Korean peninsula and grouped into four regions, comprises 63 individual tombs, 16 of which feature wall paintings. The tombs represent the full typology of Koguryo tombs from the later kingdom and together with the wall paintings represent among the only remains of the now-vanished Koguryo culture.

Most of the known tombs suffered clandestine excavations in the last thousand years and few were scientifically excavated prior to such activity. Although some of the wall paintings in the tombs were damaged by looting and environmental factors, the architectural features remain largely intact and the wall paintings possess sufficient integrity to express their Outstanding Universal Value.

The natural environment and setting of the tombs have not been substantially altered since the time the tombs were constructed, providing a clear understanding of the relationship between the tombs and their symbolic siting in the landscape.

The attributes that express the Outstanding Universal Value of the property are not threatened by development or neglect. The wall paintings and the architectural structures are vulnerable to humidity, harmful bacteria and natural weathering. There is a risk of flooding in one of the tombs and an overall plan for the management of tourism is required.

**Authenticity**

The authenticity of the tombs has been well preserved, as has their relationship with their landscape setting. The tombs have remained largely unaltered since the time of their construction and still retain the evidence of outstanding architectural techniques. The wall paintings inside are authentic and untouched.

Although parts of the wall paintings were damaged owing to looting and other factors, a significant proportion of all the attributes expressing their Outstanding Universal Value, for example, their subject matter, composition, layout, methods of portrayal, and types and texture of pigments, still remain in their original state, guaranteeing their truthfulness.

New additions to the exterior of the tombs for the purposes of protection, presentation and interpretation of the sites can be read as contemporary features that neither mimic the authentic attributes of the property, nor compromise the cultural value of the tombs.

**Protection and management requirements**

The Complex of Koguryo Tombs is substantially protected under the Law of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea on the Protection of Cultural Property. The on-site management bodies, under the guidance of the National Bureau for Cultural Property Conservation, are responsible for the conservation and management of these properties. The site management structure is adequate and staff well qualified. Buffer zones have been demarcated for all properties, and the overall state of conservation of the property is relatively good.

Conservation and restoration projects for the wall paintings of the Koguryo tombs are being undertaken in collaboration with UNESCO, notably in the Susan-ri Tomb. The major problem in the management and conservation of the tombs is the damage to the wall paintings and architectural structures done by humidity, harmful bacteria and natural weathering. To address this, a remote interior monitoring system and temperature and humidity sensor and regulation system to monitor and regulate the interior of the tombs are being planned in collaboration with UNESCO, and will be installed within a few years. Long-term strategies have been developed to conserve and restore all tombs within the serial property. This will include preventative conservation to avoid the flaking off of paint, changes to the colour of the paintings and corrosion of the tomb structures. It will also aim to continue and strengthen scientific and technical research in relevant fields. The Management Plan is being revised in order to improve conservation, management and interpretation of the property and all the associated elements, including their surrounding natural environment.

27.title: Anak Tomb No. 3
27.content:
Anak Tomb No. 3
[![Image 1: Painting of Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou in a sitting position inside a small room, with another man standing at the left](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/Man_-_Anak_Tomb_No._3.jpg/250px-Man_-_Anak_Tomb_No._3.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Man_-_Anak_Tomb_No._3.jpg)
Korean name
[Chosŏn'gŭl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangul "Hangul")안악삼호무덤
[Hancha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanja "Hanja")安岳三號墳
[Revised Romanization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revised_Romanization_of_Korean "Revised Romanization of Korean")_Anak-samho-mudeom_
[McCune–Reischauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCune%E2%80%93Reischauer "McCune–Reischauer")_Anak-samho-mudŏm_

**Anak Tomb No. 3** is a [chamber tomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamber_tomb "Chamber tomb") of [Goguryeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goguryeo "Goguryeo") located in [Anak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_(North_Korea) "Anak (North Korea)"), [South Hwanghae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Hwanghae "South Hwanghae"), [North Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Korea "North Korea"). It is known for mural paintings and an epitaph. It is part of the [Complex of Koguryo Tombs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_of_Koguryo_Tombs "Complex of Koguryo Tombs").

It was discovered in 1949 with valuable treasures stolen, but murals in good condition.

Epitaph and its interpretation
------------------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anak_Tomb_No._3&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Epitaph and its interpretation")]

The Anak Tomb No.3 is one of few Goguryeo tombs that have epitaphs so that their dates can be determined. Its seven-lined epitaph contains the date 357, the personal name Dong Shou (冬壽), his title, his birthplace and his age at death.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-bm-1) Accordingly, some scholars generally regard this site as the tomb of Dong Shou.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-bm-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:2-2) The inscription of Dong Shou relates that he was a general from the Xianbei state of [Former Yan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Former_Yan "Former Yan") in Liaodong (modern [Liaoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liaoning "Liaoning"), China), who fled to Goguryeo in 336 and was given a position in the former territory of the [Lelang commandery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lelang_commandery "Lelang commandery").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-Archived_copy-3) According to the Chinese scholar Yeh Pai who deciphered the inscription in 1951, the Dong Shou the epitaph refers to was a refugee from Liaodong who fled the Xianbei invasions in 337 and appeared in two Chinese histories, the _[Book of Jin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book\_of\_Jin "Book of Jin")_ and _[Zizhi Tongjian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zizhi\_Tongjian "Zizhi Tongjian")_. Yeh Pai's conclusions were accepted in the 1958 formal Korean report; however some Korean scholars still maintained that the tomb belongs to King Mi-chon.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:2-2) While K. H. J. Gardiner and Wonyong Kim believe this to be a Chinese tomb of excellent quality, North and other South Korean scholars believe that Dong Shou was an emigre official. Moreover, the quality of these paintings and the size of the tomb indicate that it is a royal tomb of Koguryo—a theory advocated recently by Hwi-joon Ahn and Youngsook Pak.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-Archived_copy-3) North Korean scholars claim that it is the mausoleum of [King Micheon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Micheon_of_Goguryeo "King Micheon of Goguryeo") or [King Gogugwon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Gogugwon_of_Goguryeo "King Gogugwon of Goguryeo").

The epitaph reflects a complex situation in which Dong Shou, and Goguryeo, were put. He claimed various titles including "Minister of [Lelang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lelang_Commandery "Lelang Commandery")" and "Governor of [Changli](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Changli_Commandery&action=edit&redlink=1 "Changli Commandery (page does not exist)"), [Xuantu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xuantu_Commandery "Xuantu Commandery") and [Daifang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daifang_Commandery "Daifang Commandery")." It is not clear whether these titles were given by the Eastern Jin or just self-designation. Scholars associate one of his title "Minister of Lelang" with the title "Duke of Lelang", which was bestowed on King Gogugwon by [Murong Jun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murong_Jun "Murong Jun") of the Former Yan in 354.

*   [![Image 2: Man (owner of the tomb)](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/Man_-_Anak_Tomb_No._3.jpg/120px-Man_-_Anak_Tomb_No._3.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Man_-_Anak_Tomb_No._3.jpg "Man (owner of the tomb)")

Man (owner of the tomb)

*   [![Image 3: Woman (wife of the owner)](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/An3_woman.jpg/120px-An3_woman.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:An3_woman.jpg "Woman (wife of the owner)")

Woman (wife of the owner)

*   [![Image 4: Procession Scene](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Dongshouprocessionmural.jpg/120px-Dongshouprocessionmural.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dongshouprocessionmural.jpg "Procession Scene")

Procession Scene

*   [![Image 5: Indoor Life Painting](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Anakkitchen.jpg/120px-Anakkitchen.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anakkitchen.jpg "Indoor Life Painting")

Indoor Life Painting

The Anak Tomb No. 3 is the host to multiple famous mural paintings, each giving a greater insight to the life and hierarchy of the Goguryeo people. It contains two portraits, one on the front wall of the west side chamber and one on the southern wall, portraying a man and a woman, respectively.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:0-4) Scholars have disputed the owner of this tomb and thus the identity of people portrayed in these murals; because of the epitaph, many believe that the images depict Dong Shou, a refugee from [Former Yan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Former_Yan "Former Yan"), and his wife, while others believe that the person depicted was the Goguryeo king, [King Gogukwon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gogugwon_of_Goguryeo "Gogugwon of Goguryeo").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:0-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:1-5) The man in the mural is shown to be sitting upright and is flanked by other men who are smaller than him. He is dressed in red silk clothes with a white _kwan_[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-6) over a black inner _kwan_ and is staring straight out with an impersonal expression.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:1-5) The painting of the woman resides on the southern wall of the tomb, next to that of the man, and her sitting position is slightly turned in to face him.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:0-4) The woman also wears an impersonal expression, but with a notable face shape; her face, as well as the faces of the women who flank her, is round and full, different from the typical facial structure of the Goguryeo people, who had long and oval faces.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:1-5) The woman is however wearing Chinese set of attire called [guiyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swallow-tailed_Hems_and_Flying_Ribbons_clothing "Swallow-tailed Hems and Flying Ribbons clothing"), which is a multi-lap swallow-tail clothing;[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:3-8) this reflects Chinese influences in the tomb and may indicate the clothing style worn in the Chinese [six dynasties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six_Dynasties "Six Dynasties").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-Archived_copy-3) The woman's hairstyle is identical to the hairstyle in Northern Wei.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:3-8)

The next mural in this tomb is a [procession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Procession "Procession") scene and resides in the corridor. It contains 250 people, including the owner of the tomb who is sitting in a cow-pulled wagon. Other Goguryeo people displayed in this mural include members of a marching band, flag bearers, maids and civil officials. The large number of people suggests the high social status of the owner.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:0-4) It is also important to note the seemingly identical, impersonal facial structure of the people included in this scene. This can be attributed to the fact that at the time when this mural was developed, the expression of individuality was not yet a developed technique in Goguryeo paintings.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:1-5)

The inside of the eastern chamber contains a colorful mural illustrating the typical life of the Goguryeo people. The scene includes a kitchen, a meat storage room, a barn, a carriage shed, and household staff, along with other commonplace features.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:0-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anak_Tomb_No._3#cite_note-:1-5) This mural allows scholars to analyze the daily rituals of the Goguryeo culture, and gain insight on what the house of the tomb's owner may have looked like.
